description: The phone app's one window (SPEC §4.15). It opens links in the person's browser, like the desktop list window, and calls only the app's own commands a text-only phone uses: the sign-ins, the gateway connections (gateway_retry tries one again at once when the app comes back to the screen), the start-up check (graphics_started, which does nothing off Linux), its own version for Settings (app_version, which installs nothing), and its sounds (src/phone_sound.rs): the phone's ringer, which chimes follow, a chime played as a notification sound (sound_play, the desktop's call, limited the same way), and the buzz in place of one on vibrate; and the phone's Font size (src/phone_text.rs), which the page sizes its text and rows by. And link_offered (#607, src/deep_link.rs): a linger:// link from an invite page's "Open in Linger", read strictly and turned into the link a person would paste, for the paste box. And phone_call_bar (#429, src/phone_call.rs): while in voice, the one notification the phone shows, which keeps the call going with the phone locked. And phone_save (#703, src/phone_save.rs): on an iPhone, where a download handed to the browser showed nothing, the shell fetches a shared file itself, from a web address only (checked in Rust too), into the app's temporary folder, and shows the share sheet for it; the bytes never reach the page, and the file goes when the sheet closes. Android's downloads go to the browser, so there it only refuses. Voice itself runs in the page, on the web engine's own WebRTC, and reaches the server through gateway_send, so no voice command is here. No other notifications, no updates, no other windows: lib.rs's phone_app registers nothing else, and src/acl.rs checks the two agree. The desktop files say "platforms" so none of them applies here.
